output.reason: Localized poison ivy dermatitis with active spreading rash warrants clinician assessment for appropriate topical and systemic treatment options today, but no emergent features or time-critical instability present.

Localized poison ivy dermatitis on forearms with no systemic symptoms (fever, respiratory distress) or airway involvement; self-care guidance with supportive medications and a safety net for worsening or spread to face/genitals.
output.patientMessage: Wash exposed skin and clothing thoroughly with soap and water now. Over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and antihistamines (e.g., hydroxyzine) reduce itching; topical ointments work better on blistered areas. Contact your clinician if the rash spreads beyond your forearms, involves your face, causes breathing difficulty, or worsens despite treatment.
